facts.title: July painted as a charge
facts.body: Delacroix’s Liberty Leading the People (1830) commemorates the July Revolution — Liberty herself strides over barricades with the tricolour.

facts.title: Marianne with a Phrygian cap
facts.body: Liberty, bare-breasted and purposeful, wears the Phrygian cap of freed slaves and leads mixed classes into the smoke.

facts.title: The tricolour raised
facts.body: Blue, white, and red snap above the charge — the republic’s colors made into motion.

facts.title: A child of the barricade
facts.body: A street boy with pistols — often linked to Hugo’s later Gavroche — embodies youthful fury in the revolt.

facts.title: Bourgeois beside the worker
facts.body: A top-hatted man with a hunting shotgun fights beside laborers — Delacroix paints class alliance for a day.

facts.title: Bodies underfoot
facts.body: The dead and wounded carpet the foreground — victory bought in flesh.

facts.title: Paris on the skyline
facts.body: Notre-Dame’s towers pin the scene to Paris even as smoke blurs the city.

facts.title: Powder and cloud
facts.body: Gun smoke softens the distance — history seen through a haze of combat.

facts.title: Steel at the ready
facts.body: Muskets and bayonets angle toward Liberty’s stride — the tools of the uprising.
